title: checks-<walker>.json
description: What one certifier walked, one file per walker. Written by certifier-e2e, read by certifier-auditor and by the report generator. Verdict and method values are canonical tokens; the words a reader sees come from the report's strings, so a project can localise them without touching this contract.

walker.description: The walker's id, as in the file name: w1, w2. The orchestrator uses w0 for defects it logs itself.

commit.description: Short hash of the commit certified (git rev-parse --short HEAD in the walker's checkout).

id.description: Journey id from the plan, e.g. J01. The same id may appear in two walkers' files; the generator merges them.
<journey>.<n>, unique across every walker: J01.1, J01.2.

title.description: The idea proved, twelve words or fewer, in the report's language.

users.description: Every test user whose screen appears in the evidence, by role, never a real person.

method.description: screen: seen by the user who acted. cross: the effect seen on another user's screen (the note names who acted and who saw). api: HTTP status and body read directly. seed: seeded data read as is.

verdict.description: PASS: seen, and the screenshot shows it. PARTIAL: only part holds, or it was proved in a reduced form (the note names the substitution). FAIL: the screen contradicts the expected result, or a request fails behind a cheerful screen. UNVERIFIABLE: the moment could not be reached (the note names the blocker).

cases.description: Bench case ids this check covers. Every case assigned to the walker appears in some check.

screenshots.description: Required non-empty for every verdict except UNVERIFIABLE.

file.description: Path relative to this JSON file: <journey>/<nn><letter>-<slug>-<desktop|phone>.png. The generator fails if it does not exist.

caption.description: Ten words or fewer: what the image shows, not what the walker hoped.

device.description: Optional; inferred from a -phone suffix in the file name.

note.description: Twenty-five words or fewer, only when it adds something: the substitution behind a PARTIAL, the blocker behind an UNVERIFIABLE, who acted and who saw in a cross check.

steps.description: Who, where, what they did: enough to reproduce.

expected.description: What the spec promises (the spec, not the bench, when they disagree).

screenshot.description: One image that shows it, relative to this file.

consumedState.description: What the walk spent that does not come back: approvals, sales, closed records, invitations used.

consoleNetwork.description: Console errors and failed requests seen, and which of them were expected.

unverifiable.description: Rows that could not be walked and why, or None.
